newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Wisconsin Energy back to basics.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Wisconsin Energy back to basics.

text.p: Wisconsin Energy Co's chief Richard Abdoo said the company has shifted its focus back to core operations after a proposed merger with Northern States Power Co was scuttled by regulators earlier this year.
"We have these things over the next six months we have to clean up," Abdoo told Reuters Wednesday.
In that period, Wisconsin Energy aims to bring its Point Beach nuclear power plant back to service and file to get electric rates back to levels before the merger proposal, Abdoo said.
The two Point Beach units, in Two Rivers, Wis., were shut for refueling and kept down due to safety concerns raised by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).
Last Friday, NRC granted approval to restart the units.
The 485 MW unit 2, which has been shut since October for refueling and replacement of steam generators, will likely put electricity back on the grid by the weekend.
The adjoining unit 1, also at 485 MW, should restart within two to three weeks of unit 2 reaching full power. The unit has been off line since February for refueling and maintenance.

The unexpected, lengthy outages have been costly for Wisconsin Energy. The company has spent roughly $10 million each month, mostly in the spot market, to buy power to compensate for the loss of the Point Beach plant.

Before analysts today, Abdoo said costs related to the Point Beach outage as well as a one-time write-off for the failed merger would result in a second quarter loss in the range of seven to 12 cents a share compared with a profit of 41 cents for the same period a year earlier.
Analysts had expected a Q2 profit of 30 cents a share.
Wisconsin Energy, based in Milwaukee, and Northern States, headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on May 16 called off its $6 billion merger to form a company called Primergy Corp.
Wisconsin Energy planned to release its second quarter earnings Wednesday July 30 after its board meeting.

As a requirement to gain approval from state regulators for the merger with Northern States Power, Wisconsin Energy agreed to slash its electric rates by $42 million last year and $14 million this year.
Wisconsin Energy's subsidiary, Wisconsin Electric Power Co, serves about 2.3 million people in southeastern Wisconsin.
"We want to restore our (rate) levels before the decreases...and recover for Point Beach's maintenance costs and increased operating costs," Abdoo said.
According to Abdoo, Wisconsin Energy planned to file for a 10 percent rate hike with the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin in mid-August. Details of the filing were not yet available.
He said the company has not yet encountered customer opposition for the planned rate hike, adding it still has some of the lowest electric prices in the country.
"Our industrial customers say 'We like your service and you can't beat the price'," Abdoo said.

After getting the company's operations and finances in order, Abdoo said he will turn his attention to look for joint ventures, consolidations and/or possible acquisitions after learning from the cancelled merger with Northern States.
"Our strategy was superb but our execution was terrible," Abdoo said of the failed merger attempt.
((--New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622))
